statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 14 of 100 in the low band, eleven points below the 25-point block threshold, because CME equity index futures remain inside the regular weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday and no Nasdaq-100 price path exists to be pathological. Ten of the twenty-four forward slots sit inside that closure. Stress rises to 67 in the high band: a Russian drone struck a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train two kilometres from the Polish border early Sunday and Poland activated air-defence systems, adding a second unpriced weekend vector to the Hormuz vessel strike, alongside oil above $100, a 10-year near 4.95 per cent and a Fed decision on Wednesday at which a 25 basis point increase is broadly priced. The one structural checkpoint inside the horizon is the scheduled 22:00 UTC restart, published as a narrow danger window running to 03:00 UTC on Monday rather than a broad session-wide state change.
recommendation: Tail sits in the low band, so the deterministic repository mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and this single shared reading applies jointly to NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support it. First, no venue quotes the Nasdaq-100 in ten of the twenty-four published forward slots: CME equity index futures closed at 21:00 UTC on Friday for the weekend and are scheduled to resume at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, so there is no gap, no failed retracement and no session extreme available to score. Second, the weekend record is now two-vector and severe, but it is carried in Stress rather than Tail, because Tail measures a pathological price path and no path currently exists to be pathological; the record is also two-sided, with Monday's Salalah meeting on temporary Hormuz shipping lanes set against the vessel strike, and with Polish operational command reporting no violation of Polish airspace. Third, the five watch-band slots from 22:00 UTC on Sunday to 03:00 UTC on Monday are published as a narrow evidence-based danger window rather than a broad shutdown, and even the peak conditional Tail of 24 stays one point below the block threshold. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this reading.
headline: With CME equity index futures in their regular weekend closure the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX at 15.84, while a Russian drone hit a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train two kilometres from the Polish border during a 453-drone overnight assault that killed six across Ukraine, and an Iranian commercial ship was struck near Qeshm in the Strait of Hormuz with one dead; Tail stays at 14 because there is no live price path to score, and the published risk is concentrated in the 22:00 UTC restart.
body:
Last observed tape. The Nasdaq-100 closed Friday at 29,368.44, up 0.91 per cent from a 29,103.51 previous close, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 day range. VIX fell 11.21 per cent to 15.84 from a 17.71 intraday high. That was a relief session that recovered part of the preceding decline, and it is two-sided, mean-reverting behaviour rather than one-way structure, which is why the published dominant mode is normal.

Cross-asset state. WTI settled at $100.05, down 2.37 per cent on Friday, with Brent at $104.61, down 2.81 per cent; the pullback followed Iranian state media confirming that Tehran would meet Gulf states in Oman on the Strait of Hormuz. Dated Brent has traded above $100 since 3 September. H.15 for 10 September shows the 2-year Treasury at 4.56 per cent and the 10-year at 4.95 per cent. Crude above $100 alongside a recovering equity tape is a conflict rather than an alignment, and conflicting cross-asset signals raise Stress more than Tail. Delayed latest-session context is consistent with that reading: Nasdaq futures +0.86 per cent, VIX futures -8.41 per cent, seven of eight megacaps higher and a semiconductor mean of +1.75 per cent, all of which confirm Friday's close and none of which is evidence of a current price path.

Weekend record, first vector. An Iranian commercial vessel was struck early Sunday off Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, with one of ten crew killed and four wounded. The Qeshm governor blamed a hostile actor per state-run IRNA, and the U.S. military offered no immediate comment. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations monitor reported a vessel hit by a projectile while transiting the strait. Gulf Cooperation Council diplomats and Iraq are expected to meet their Iranian counterpart in Oman on Monday on a temporary arrangement for managing shipping through the waterway, with Bahrain declining to attend. That meeting is a scheduled checkpoint, not a result.

Weekend record, second vector. A Russian drone struck the locomotive of a Kyiv-Warsaw passenger train roughly two kilometres from the Polish border in Volyn early Sunday, with no injuries after the crew was warned in advance, and a drone also hit a filling station near the Yahodyn-Dorohusk crossing. Russia launched 453 drones plus decoys and missiles overnight, heavily targeting western Ukraine; attacks across the country killed at least six civilians and injured 43. Poland activated air-defence and reconnaissance systems and issued alerts in border counties, and Lithuania scrambled NATO jets. Polish operational command reported no violation of Polish airspace and the Polish interior ministry reported no injuries on the Polish side. This is a proximity escalation toward NATO territory without, so far, a NATO-territory incident.

Why Tail stays low. Tail measures the probability of a price path that denies meaningful mean reversion. The reference contract has been shut since 21:00 UTC Friday and is scheduled to resume at 22:00 UTC Sunday, so for ten of the twenty-four forward slots there is no path to score at all. None of the amplifiers that would justify a Tail of 25 or more is observable: there is no gap, no shallow-pullback sequence, no repeated extension after failed retracements and no holding near a session extreme. Two independent unpriced geopolitical vectors and a hawkish rate backdrop are exactly the conditions the model carries in Stress and in the restart window rather than in current Tail.

Scheduled catalysts. The FOMC decision and Summary of Economic Projections land at 18:00 UTC on Wednesday 16 September with the Chair's press conference at 18:30 UTC, and market-implied odds of a 25 basis point increase were around 86 per cent after Friday's core CPI print. Retail Sales for August arrive at 12:30 UTC the same morning, and Initial Jobless Claims and the Philadelphia Fed index at 12:30 UTC on Thursday. The Monday U.S. calendar is thin, limited to 3-month and 6-month bill auctions. FOMC is a structurally multi-stage sequence, and it sits outside this twenty-four hour horizon; it is carried in the event calendar and in Stress, not in current Tail.

Published risk shape. The danger window runs from the scheduled 22:00 UTC restart to 03:00 UTC on Monday, the five slots where conditional Tail enters the watch band with a peak of 24. That peak is one point below the block threshold, and no forward slot in this horizon reaches the block band.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 12:00 UTC on 12 September to 11:00 UTC on 13 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The whole window sits inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday. Tail held at 6 for the first seventeen slots, then stepped to 7 at 05:00 UTC, 8 at 06:00, 9 at 07:00, 10 at 08:00, 11 at 09:00, 12 at 10:00 and 13 at 11:00 on 13 September, tracking elapsed time without price discovery rather than any observed structure. Stress traced a shallow U: it eased from 54 to 50 between 12:00 and 17:00 UTC on 12 September as Friday's relief close and the crude pullback were absorbed, then rebuilt to 66 by 11:00 UTC on 13 September as the weekend Hormuz, Yemen and now Ukraine record accumulated. Confidence stayed between 85 and 87 throughout. Every slot mapped to EA_ON and green in normal mode, so no lookback hour reached the watch band.
outlookSummary: Ten of the twenty-four forward slots lie inside the CME weekend closure; the reference contract is scheduled to resume at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, this horizon's eleventh slot. Conditional Tail opens at 14 in the current slot, the only slot describing observed rather than hypothetical conditions, and drifts to 19 by 20:00 UTC as unpriced weekend exposure accumulates across two independent vectors. It is capped at 19 through the closure because a shut contract cannot show the one-way structure Tail measures. The restart slot carries the horizon's peak at 24, the top of the watch band and one point below the block threshold, because the first prints would have to absorb a Hormuz vessel strike, a NATO-border drone escalation and Monday's Salalah diplomacy simultaneously in thin liquidity. Tail then decays to 19 by 03:00 UTC on the assumption of orderly two-sided price discovery, and the published danger window is deliberately limited to 22:00 UTC Sunday through 03:00 UTC Monday rather than the whole Monday session. Stress stays in the high band in every slot, between 66 and 71, and leads Tail throughout because a likely Fed hike, oil above $100, a 10-year near 4.95 per cent and two active conflicts are event importance rather than observed price structure. Confidence falls to 81 by the last closure hour on staleness, troughs at 78 in the thin restart hour and recovers to 85 by Monday morning on the assumption that a full overnight path is then available to score.
